sentences.text: Ticinosuchus was a medium-sized, crocodile-like carnivore covered in a shell of small bony plates that protected its body and tail.
This powerful animal measured approximately 3 meters in length.
A specialized calcaneus and ankle joint likely made Ticinosuchus a fast runner, unlike many primitive reptiles.
Ticinosuchus is one of the few terrestrial animals found in the Besano Formation, a site famous for its marine fossils.
The genus name Ticinosuchus means "Ticino crocodile" because it was discovered in the Swiss canton of Ticino.
The genus Ticinosuchus was described by Krebs in 1965, and the only known species is Ticinosuchus ferox.
The presence of sharp and recurved teeth indicates that Ticinosuchus had a carnivorous diet.
Anatomical features shared with other archosaurs indicate that Ticinosuchus moved with a fully erect, quadrupedal gait.
Ticinosuchus is classified within the family Prestosuchidae.
Ticinosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic, spanning the Anisian to Ladinian stages, in Switzerland and Italy.
